Class CellContext

java.lang.Object
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.render.CellContext
public abstract class CellContext extends Object

Everything a CellRenderer needs to paint one cell or one column header. The grid fills in one instance and reuses it for every cell, so painting does not allocate. Bounds exclude the grid lines. Font, text fill and alignment already include the cell style.

The grid provides the implementation; a test of a renderer can provide its own.

    • isSelected

      public abstract boolean isSelected()
      Whether the cell is painted as selected; its background is already painted. While the grid has the focus, the focused cell of a selection of several cells is painted as not selected (except in row mode), so its border stands out.

    • isFocused

      public abstract boolean isFocused()
      Whether the cell has the keyboard focus; its border is painted afterwards.

    • isEditable

      public boolean isEditable()
      Whether the user can edit the cell in place: the grid is editable and the model allows it. A context that does not override this, such as one in a renderer test, says true.

    • getFractionDigits

      public int getFractionDigits()
      The fraction digits CellRenderers.NUMBER shows at least, so that decimal separators line up: the most any decimal number on screen in this column needs. 0 for headers and for a context that does not override this.

    • fitText

      public String fitText(String text)
      Shortens text with an ellipsis so it fits between the paddings in the cell's font. The grid remembers the full text for the tooltip and its width for fitting the column.

    • fitText

      public abstract String fitText(String text, javafx.scene.text.Font font)
      Like fitText(String), for text drawn in another font than the cell's, such as a smaller second line in a header. Fitting the column counts this text too. If several texts of a cell are cut off, the tooltip shows the first one.
      Parameters:
      text - the text to fit
      font - the font the renderer draws text with
      Returns:
      text, or a prefix plus an ellipsis, or "" if not even the ellipsis fits

    • wrapText

      public abstract List<String> wrapText(String text)
      Wraps text into as many lines as fit the cell's height, each fitting between the paddings. If the text needs more lines, the last one ends in an ellipsis and the grid remembers the full text for the tooltip.

    • getLineHeight

      public abstract double getLineHeight()
      Height of one line of text in the current font.

    • indent

      public abstract void indent(double width)
      Moves the start of the cell's content right by width, for something a renderer paints before it, such as an icon or the indentation of a tree. getX() and getWidth() change accordingly, fitText(String) fits into what is left, and fitting the column to its content counts the width.
      Parameters:
      width - the space taken at the left

    • snap

      public double snap(double position)
      The nearest position on the screen's pixel grid, taking zoom and display scaling into account. Lines and boxes drawn between snapped positions stay sharp. Without a grid (a test context) positions are rounded to whole numbers.
      Parameters:
      position - an x or y coordinate in the cell's coordinate system
      Returns:
      the snapped coordinate
